# s446 — Vague Check section: warn when a slice has no verifiable acceptance criteria

An advisory, never a block: `slicer check` and `slicer promote` warn when a live slice's Check section has no backticked command line and no `[HUMAN CHECK]` line, or its Failing tests section names no backticked test. The slice template and `docs/agents.md` tell authors to write each check as a command with its expected result, or a `[HUMAN CHECK]` that says what to look at and what to see.

**Findings:** Owner 2026-11-03 (from ork): slicer and ork should both encourage well defined acceptance criteria for every slice. Fact: S102 (done) blocks `slicer next` only when Implement or Check is empty, and its Not in this slice says a short Check is not refused. Needed: an advisory (not a block) from slicer check, promote or show when a slice Check or Failing tests have no command, expected result or observable outcome; and the slice template and docs/agents.md guidance tell authors to write acceptance criteria that way. Open: what counts as vague, and whether it is a warning in check, in next, or only in the template. · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

## Why

Owner 2026-11-03 (from ork): slicer and ork should both encourage well defined acceptance criteria for every slice. ork's side landed as ork S278 (its spec check asks the owner to tighten a vague Check). S102 (done) holds a slice back from `slicer next` only when Implement or Check is empty, and its Not in this slice says a short Check is not refused, so a Check of "tests pass" or "works as described" goes through.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-05 (interview in the ork session):

1. Vague means: the Check section has no line that holds a backticked command and no line that holds `[HUMAN CHECK]`; or the Failing tests section names no backticked test. Text only; slicer does not judge whether a command's expected result is written.
2. Where: a warning in `slicer check` (exit status unchanged) and in `slicer promote` output for that slice, plus the slice template and `docs/agents.md` guidance. It stays advisory everywhere.

What the code shows (read 2026-11-05): `check` gathers warnings in `src/slicer/check.py:81-96` (offline findings at level warn, then sibling collisions, gitignore lines, prompt warnings and the pin mismatch); warnings never change the exit status. `promote` prints one line, "promoted ID -> PATH" (`src/slicer/cli_track.py:287-298`). The slice template is `src/slicer/templates/slice.md`.
